statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The Iranian retaliation wave that the previous hours flagged as the main unresolved overnight mechanism has now printed — 13 ballistic missiles at Jordan with 10 intercepted, drones repelled by Kuwait and Bahrain, no casualties or damage reported — and index futures absorbed it without a directional break. NQ traded 29,132.25 at 23:15 UTC, above its 29,125.50 pre-halt reference. Tail holds at 20 rather than decaying, because a larger U.S. counter-response has been threatened and is unresolved.
recommendation: The overnight escalation that had been the principal conditional risk has now occurred and has been absorbed. More than an hour into the reopen, the Nasdaq-100 contract is +0.02% inside a 29,103.25-29,149.00 band and back above its pre-halt reference, the S&P 500 contract is +0.04% across a 6.5-point band, and WTI is $90.83 in a 43-cent range rather than extending. Stress stays high at 74 because the conflict is unresolved, a ceasefire has been publicly ruled out, and a larger U.S. response has been threatened after Iran's retaliation. Mapped policy state: WATCH, with the danger window left on the 13:30-14:30 UTC U.S. cash open on 2 September; the 22:00 UTC futures reopen that follows Broadcom's results is the secondary checkpoint.
headline: Iran's retaliation wave lands and is absorbed: Nasdaq-100 futures hold +0.02% above the pre-halt reference while a threatened larger U.S. response keeps Stress high at 74
body:
The defining development of this hour is that the escalation the previous assessments identified as the key unresolved mechanism has actually occurred, and the market did not break on it. Between roughly 20:35 and 22:42 UTC, sirens sounded in Jordan's Mafraq and Aqaba regions, Jordan intercepted 10 of 13 ballistic missiles launched from Iran with three others landing in remote areas and no casualties reported, Kuwait and Bahrain activated air defences against incoming drones with no reported injuries or damage, and U.S. Central Command announced that its own wave of strikes on IRGC air defence sites, radar, maritime assets and communications facilities was complete.

Index futures absorbed all of it. At 23:15 UTC the Nasdaq-100 contract printed 29,132.25, +0.02%, inside a 29,103.25 to 29,149.00 reopen band and roughly seven points above the 29,125.50 pre-halt reference. The S&P 500 contract was 7,645.50, +0.04%, across a 6.5-point band. WTI was $90.83, +0.68%, in a $90.57 to $91.00 range — holding its earlier advance rather than extending on the retaliation. That is a full hour of the thinnest liquidity of the day meeting a confirmed multi-country missile and drone exchange and producing no gap, no directional break and no session-extreme holding. It is direct evidence against the pathological no-retracement path.

The reason Tail holds at 20 rather than easing further is the other half of the picture. A ceasefire has been publicly ruled out, and a substantially larger U.S. response was threatened in the event of Iranian retaliation. Iran has now retaliated. That leaves a credible, unresolved second-leg mechanism live across the overnight hours, which is why the projected path in this assessment is lifted relative to the previous hour: the overnight trough moves from 16 to 18 rather than decaying into the low teens.

Cross-asset confirmation remains mixed rather than aligned, which is the main reason Tail sits well below the blocking threshold. VIX finished the cash session at 16.34, up 9.5% but only to a low absolute level for a day carrying direct strikes. The 31 August H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.75% and the 30-year at 5.25%; the 1 September release has not yet posted. Megacap performance was genuinely split rather than uniform, with Apple +2.61% and Meta +1.08% against Nvidia -1.51%, Amazon -1.87% and Tesla -3.22%. Semiconductors were broadly but not uniformly weaker, with AMD -2.36%, Micron -2.64% and Arm -2.93% against Broadcom -0.18%. Sector breadth was negative across technology, communication services and consumer cyclicals, but uniform negative breadth after a headline shock is a Stress input, not evidence of directional efficiency.

The cash session itself was structurally two-sided. The Nasdaq-100 closed 1.29% lower at 29,077.22 inside a 28,953.26 to 29,267.42 range, having broken and reclaimed its session low, and the S&P 500 finished -0.71% at 7,631.47. Today's macro block was mildly soft and is behind: ISM Manufacturing at 54.6 against 55.2 expected, and JOLTS openings at 7.271 million against 7.3 million.

One new scheduled catalyst has been verified and added to the calendar. Broadcom reports third-quarter fiscal 2026 results after the U.S. close on 2 September, with the conference call confirmed for 21:00 UTC. That lands inside the CME index futures maintenance halt, so the print reprices at the 22:00 UTC reopen into the thinnest liquidity of the day. The forecast reflects this: the final slot is raised to 22 rather than the 18 that a purely geopolitical overnight would have carried.

Stress therefore stays high at 74 while Tail holds at 20. The structure that would change this reading is unchanged: an unretraced break of the 29,103.25 reopen low or the 28,953.26 cash low followed by repeated extension after failed pullbacks. Nothing observed through this assessment cutoff shows it.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-two of the 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 15:00 and 20:00 UTC hours on 1 September have none and are marked unavailable. The first nine slots, covering the late 31 August session and the overnight into 1 September, sat in the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 11 and mode mixed, while Stress drifted from 50 up to 58. The regime broke at 08:00 UTC as the Hormuz escalation reached the tape: Tail jumped to 22 with mode trend-down, then held the 25-31 orange band from 09:00 through 13:00 UTC and peaked at 31 with Stress 75 around the U.S. cash open. From 14:00 UTC the tape turned two-sided and mode switched to event/whipsaw, with Tail oscillating between 21 and 25 through the rest of the cash session; 19:00 UTC returned briefly to 25 on the session-low break, and the last two available hours eased to 21 and then 20 as the futures reopen printed without a gap.
outlookSummary: The projection opens at 20 for the current 23:00 UTC hour, unchanged from the previous assessment rather than decaying, because the Iranian retaliation wave has now printed and been absorbed while a larger U.S. counter-response remains threatened and unresolved. It holds 20 through the Tokyo and Seoul cash open, eases to 19 across the Asian session and to a projected overnight trough of 18 between 04:00 and 06:00 UTC — a trough deliberately lifted from the 16 carried in the previous hour, because a live and unresolved escalation ladder does not support a deeper overnight decay. It stays at 18-19 through the European reopening and the quiet European stretch, then rises into the U.S. data block: 20 ahead of the 12:15 UTC ADP release, 21 at the release, 22 at the cash open and a projected peak of 24 for the 14:00 UTC hour, which is the declared 13:30-14:30 UTC danger window. It fades to 22, 20 and 19 through the midday lull, holds at 19 across the 18:00 UTC Beige Book, lifts to 20 for the power hour and holds 20 into the 20:00 UTC cash close, where Broadcom's third-quarter results are due. The 21:00 UTC CME maintenance halt is projected at 17 because there is no continuous discovery inside it, and the 22:00 UTC reopen is projected at 22 — materially above tonight's equivalent hour — because a megacap semiconductor repricing meets the thinnest liquidity of the day. Every forecast value beyond the current hour is conditional risk; no future price structure is asserted as observed. The whole path assumes the 29,103.25 reopen low and the 28,953.26 cash low hold, and would be re-scored quickly if either broke without retracement.
